stage_flags.note: Per rubric, all claims in Stage 3 (index <3 means stages numbered from 0 — however this is Stage 3 in content, not sub-stage) are not auto-capped; flag does not apply as this is Stage 3 content-wise; no automatic cap triggered

No claim in this stage meets the High threshold (3+ independent sources with ≥1 primary, OR 2+ with ≥1 gov/multilateral). The highest-quality evidence clusters (PP3.2 sample rejection data with 2 Malaysia-specific academic sources) reaches only Medium. The PP3.1 cost case rests on three ASSUMED-tagged claims and job-aggregator salary data.

The PP3.1 primary cost argument ('250-500 staff-hours per 1,000-employee campaign at $445-$1,395') is constructed from ASSUMED-3 (collation time) × JobStreet salary data — both Low. The error-cost layer ($33,300-$48,100) requires the JAMIA 3.7% rate (Medium, US-context) × rovinghealth $45-65/incident (Low, trade blog, US-context). The entire PP3.1 cost model is anchored in Low-confidence inputs.

Prodia OHI's '500,000 employees/year' and '>2,000 companies' figures, cited multiple times as evidence of market scale, are sourced exclusively from Prodia's own marketing pages. No audited IDX filing or independent verification cited. These figures should be treated as marketing claims only.

gate_reasoning: Stage 3 scores 0% High, 43% Medium, 57% Low across 60 claims. The most critical deficiencies are structural: (1) the entire PP3.1 direct cost model rests on ASSUMED-3 (collation time, zero sourcing) and job-aggregator salary data rather than BPS/DOSM wage surveys, making the '250-500 staff-hours' and '$445-$1,395 per campaign' figures unverifiable; (2) market size anchors (Indonesia USD 656M, Malaysia USD 284M) come exclusively from Grand View Research, an auto-downgrade aggregator with no crossvalidation from MOH health expenditure statistics, IFC private health market reports, or World Bank health financing data; (3) the foundational regulatory claim (Permenaker 02/1980 mandating annual MCU for all formal employers) cites only legal commentary blogs rather than the JDIH Kemnaker gazette; (4) Prodia scale figures (500K employees, >2,000 companies) used repeatedly as evidence of market scale are sourced entirely from Prodia's own marketing pages. PP3.2 is in better shape — Malaysia-specific academic data on sample rejection rates is solid at Medium — but even PP3.2's cost-per-incident figures are transplanted from Turkey and US studies without local calibration. Deep research should prioritize: BPS/DOSM wage data for admin staff, JDIH Kemnaker for Permenaker 02/1980 text, a time-motion study or clinical document processing benchmark for collation time, and a World Bank or ADB source to crossvalidate market sizing.
